messages:
diane-security: Heads-up — we're opening a preview for a new on‑prem troubleshooting feature: Ephemeral Support Shell (ESS).

Key points:
- ESS provides time‑limited, auditable support sessions for Private/VPC/on‑prem customers.
- Sessions are customer‑consented via the Console (explicit allow per session). Default = OFF.
- Access uses ephemeral tokens, TTL default 1 hour (configurable by customer up to 8h).
- All session metadata (who, start/end, commands run summary) is logged to the customer audit sink; no persistent shell backdoor.
- Requires agent v4.0.1+ (mandatory for the preview).
- Enterprise+ customers only for preview; we'll expand after compliance review.

Compliance/security notes: we ran this past legal and SOC2 leads — design avoids storing PII from interactive sessions, TLS + mTLS to control endpoints, and KMS‑backed signing of session tokens. More detail in the RFC and the docs linked below.

Rollout plan (high level):
- 2026-04-02: agent v4.0.1 release (optional canary).
- 2026-04-07: limited preview enablement for selected Enterprise accounts (SE invites).
- 2026-05-01: broader GA review after feedback and audit.

Action items for teams:
- Eng-runtime: ensure agent verify path + token rotation (PR #4821).
- Eng-security: run the audit checklist and provide final attestation by 2026-04-05.
- SE / PS: coordinate invites and proctor sessions with customers; use the support checklist.
- Docs / DevEx: publish a customer FAQ and Console UX help text.

Docs/refs: https://redwood.ai/docs/onprem/ephemeral-shell-preview (draft) | RFC: https://redwood.ai/rfcs/ephemeral-shell

If you're interested in being in the preview cohort or have blockers, reply here or ping me directly.

ajay-prod: Quick q — will any customers be auto‑opted in for the preview?

diane-security: No — preview is opt‑in only. SEs will invite accounts; Console toggle is OFF by default. We want an explicit customer acceptance flow recorded.

leo-sre: Tech Q — what network footprint do customers need to open? Do we require inbound ports?

diane-security: No inbound ports required. ESS initiates an outbound TLS websocket to support.redwood.ai over 443, then upgrades to an encrypted mux channel for the shell. For air‑gapped installs we provide an offline bundle and a signed replayable audit artifact instead (details in doc).

maria-ps: Will there be a customer‑facing opt‑out notice or an admin consent screen we can demo?

diane-security: Yep — Console will show a modal with the session summary, TTL, and a checkbox to allow. SE guide will include screenshots and suggested language. Draft UX is in the docs link.

devex-bot: Release notes snippet (draft): "Agent v4.0.1: Ephemeral Support Shell (preview) — adds support session handshake, token validation, and session audit hooks. See release PR: https://git.internal/redwood/agent/pull/4821"

oncall-bot: Deploy plan: canary rollout to dogfooding cluster 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC, wider canary 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC. No expected customer downtime.

ajay-prod: OK sounds good — will coordinate invites with PS next week.

leo-sre: :thumbsup:

maria-ps: +1 — please add a one‑pager for sales with the compliance bullets.

diane-security: Will do. I'll follow up with a shared checklist and the SE invite spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
